subject: Science
title: Chemical Reactions
learningOutcomes: Explain what a chemical reaction is and state the Law of Conservation of Mass.
Balance chemical equations and use the state symbols (s), (l), (g) and (aq).
Identify synthesis, decomposition, displacement, double displacement and combustion reactions.
Tell endothermic (takes in heat) from exothermic (gives out heat) reactions.
Explain how ionic and covalent bonds form, and why water is a polar molecule.

sections.heading: Chemical Reactions & Conservation of Mass
sections.body: A chemical reaction turns reactants into new products with different properties. The number of atoms never changes — none are made or lost — so the total mass of the reactants always equals the total mass of the products. This is the Law of Conservation of Mass, discovered by Antoine Lavoisier.

sections.heading: Balancing Equations & State Symbols
sections.body: A balanced equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides; you balance it by putting numbers in front of formulae. State symbols show the physical state: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas and (aq) dissolved in water.

sections.heading: Types of Reaction
sections.body: Synthesis: two substances combine into one (Fe + S → FeS). Decomposition: one compound breaks into simpler products, often using heat (CuCO₃ → CuO + CO₂). Displacement: a more reactive element pushes out a less reactive one (Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂). Double displacement: two compounds swap partners (BaCl₂ + MgSO₄ → BaSO₄ + MgCl₂). Combustion: a fuel burns in oxygen giving CO₂ and water.

sections.heading: Endothermic & Exothermic Reactions
sections.body: Endothermic reactions take in heat, so the surroundings get colder (photosynthesis, cooking, melting ice). Exothermic reactions give out heat, so the surroundings get hotter (burning, rusting, freezing water, neutralisation, respiration).

sections.heading: Ionic & Covalent Bonding
sections.body: When a metal reacts with a non-metal, electrons are transferred: the metal forms a positive ion (cation) and the non-metal a negative ion (anion). The opposite charges attract in a strong ionic bond, so ionic compounds have high melting points and conduct only when molten or dissolved. In covalent bonding, atoms share electrons; the forces between molecules are weak, so covalent compounds have low melting points and do not conduct. Water is a polar molecule — slightly + at one end and slightly − at the other — which makes it an excellent solvent.

definitions.definition: A starting substance that is used up in a reaction.
A new substance that is formed in a reaction.
Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products; no atoms are made or lost.
An equation with the same number of atoms of each element on both sides.
Two substances combining to make one new substance.
One compound breaking down into simpler products.
A more reactive element pushing out a less reactive one.
Two compounds swapping partners to form two new compounds.
Burning — a fuel reacting with oxygen, giving out heat and light.
A reaction that takes in heat (surroundings get colder).
A reaction that gives out heat (surroundings get hotter).
A positive ion — an atom that has lost electrons.
A negative ion — an atom that has gained electrons.
The strong attraction between positive and negative ions.
A shared pair of electrons between atoms.
A molecule slightly positive at one end and slightly negative at the other, e.g. water.

examTips: To balance, put numbers in FRONT of formulae — never change the small subscript numbers. Balanced = equal atoms of each element on both sides.
Endothermic takes IN heat (colder); exothermic gives OUT heat (hotter). Watch out: burning, rusting, neutralisation and respiration are all exothermic.
Metal + non-metal → ionic (electrons transferred, high melting point, conducts when molten/dissolved). Non-metals sharing electrons → covalent (low melting point, does not conduct).

interactiveLesson.instructions: Explore the key ideas of chemical reactions. Select every hotspot to continue.

hotspots.label: Reactants
hotspots.fact: The starting substances that are used up in a reaction.

hotspots.label: Products
hotspots.fact: The new substances that are made — with the same total mass as the reactants.

hotspots.label: Conservation of Mass
hotspots.fact: No atoms are made or lost, so total mass stays the same before and after.

hotspots.label: Endothermic
hotspots.fact: Takes in heat — the surroundings get colder (e.g. photosynthesis, melting ice).

hotspots.label: Exothermic
hotspots.fact: Gives out heat — the surroundings get hotter (e.g. burning, rusting, neutralisation).

practiceQuestions.prompt: What are the substances used up in a reaction called?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Reactants are used up; products are made.

practiceQuestions.prompt: What does the Law of Conservation of Mass state?

options: Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products
Mass is lost when a gas escapes
Atoms are created in a reaction

practiceQuestions.explanation: No atoms are made or lost.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Copper carbonate is heated into copper oxide and carbon dioxide. What type of reaction is this?
practiceQuestions.explanation: One compound breaks into simpler products.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Methane burns in oxygen. What type of reaction is this?
practiceQuestions.explanation: A fuel reacting with oxygen is combustion.

practiceQuestions.prompt: What gas is given off when a metal reacts with an acid?
What happens to limewater when carbon dioxide is bubbled through it?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Milky limewater is the test for CO₂.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Exothermic reactions make the surroundings colder.
practiceQuestions.explanation: False — exothermic gives out heat, so the surroundings get hotter.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A solid ionic compound conducts electricity.
practiceQuestions.explanation: False — only when molten or dissolved.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A balanced equation has equal numbers of atoms of each element on both sides.
A positive ion is called a ______.
When atoms share electrons, the bond is a ______ bond.
What happens to electrons when a metal reacts with a non-metal?

options: They are transferred from the metal to the non-metal

practiceQuestions.prompt: Why does salt dissolve easily in water?

options: Water is polar and attracts the charged ions

practiceQuestions.prompt: What is the balanced equation for methane burning in oxygen?

sequencingActivity.prompt: Arrange the steps of forming sodium chloride (an ionic bond) in the correct order.

items: The ions attract to form NaCl
correctOrder: The ions attract to form NaCl

sequencingActivity.explanation: Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine; the ions that form then attract to make NaCl.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: When marble reacts with acid in an open flask, the balance reading drops. When the same reaction is done with a balloon over the flask, the reading does not drop. Why?

options: The balloon traps the carbon dioxide, so no mass escapes — mass is conserved
Mass is created inside the balloon
Atoms are destroyed in the open flask
The acid evaporates only with a balloon

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: The gas has mass; trapping it shows mass is conserved.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A student mixes two substances and the beaker feels cold. Which correctly describes this?

options: It is exothermic — heat is given out
It is endothermic — the reaction takes in heat from the surroundings

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: Colder surroundings mean heat was taken in (endothermic).

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Magnesium oxide has a much higher melting point than sodium chloride. What is the best reason?

options: MgO ions carry double charges (Mg²⁺ and O²⁻), so the electrostatic attraction is stronger

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: Double charges = stronger attraction = higher melting point.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A substance has a low melting point, is a gas at room temperature and does not conduct electricity. What is it most likely to be?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: Low melting point + no conduction = covalent.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A colourless solution is mixed with another and a white solid settles at the bottom. Which reaction has most likely occurred?

options: A double displacement, forming an insoluble precipitate

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: A precipitate forming from two solutions is double displacement (e.g. BaSO₄).
